summary: Fine-tuning makes sense when you need to change a model's behavior, tone, or output format consistently, or encode domain-specific patterns that no prompt can reliably reproduce, whereas RAG is better when you need access to current or proprietary knowledge that changes frequently. Prompt engineering should always be your first attempt since it is free and instant, and most teams should only move to fine-tuning after prompting and RAG hit measurable quality or latency ceilings. In 2026, coding assistants and agents have become the dominant AI use case (66%), and the fine-tuning market has consolidated around managed cloud services (OpenAI, Together AI, Bedrock, Vertex) and efficient open-source frameworks (Unsloth, Axolotl, LLaMA-Factory).
when_to_fine_tune: Choose fine-tuning when you need consistent output structure, style, or tone that prompting cannot reliably enforce across thousands of requests.
Choose RAG over fine-tuning when the knowledge your model needs changes frequently or must cite specific, up-to-date source documents.
Choose fine-tuning to reduce latency and token cost by baking repeated instructions and few-shot examples directly into the model weights.
Choose fine-tuning for domain adaptation (legal, medical, financial) where specialized vocabulary and reasoning patterns must be deeply internalized rather than retrieved.

tools.name: OpenAI Fine-Tuning API
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-per-token for training and usage; GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4.1 fine-tuning billed per 1M training tokens plus inference premium over base models
features: Hosted inference with no infra management
tools.best_for: Instruction tuning and behavior/format alignment on top-tier closed models with zero infrastructure overhead

tools.name: Hugging Face AutoTrain
tools.pricing_paid: Pay for compute via Hugging Face Spaces/Inference Endpoints; local use is free
features: Broadest model selection of any platform
tools.best_for: Research and experimentation plus no-code fine-tuning across the widest range of open-source base models

tools.name: Unsloth
tools.pricing_paid: Open source and free; Pro/Enterprise tiers for multi-GPU and managed features
features: Fits large models on single consumer GPUs
tools.best_for: Cost-efficient LoRA/QLoRA fine-tuning on limited or single-GPU hardware

tools.name: Together AI
tools.pricing_paid: LoRA and full-parameter SFT from $0.48 per million training tokens; H100 clusters from $3.19/hour reserved
tools.best_for: High-performance fine-tuning plus dedicated capacity production deployment on open models

tools.name: Amazon Bedrock Fine-Tuning
tools.pricing_paid: Pay per token for training plus provisioned throughput for custom model inference
tools.best_for: Enterprise domain adaptation with strict compliance, data residency, and AWS ecosystem integration

tools.name: Vertex AI
tools.pricing_paid: Pay per node-hour for tuning jobs plus inference billing; supervised tuning priced per token for Gemini
supported_models: select open models via Model Garden
tools.best_for: Enterprise instruction tuning of Gemini and open models within the Google Cloud ecosystem

tools.name: Axolotl
tools.pricing_paid: Free and open source; you pay only for your own compute
tools.best_for: Flexible, reproducible production fine-tuning pipelines controlled via config files

tools.name: LLaMA-Factory
tools.pricing_paid: Free and open source; you pay only for your own compute
tools.best_for: Unified low-code fine-tuning across a very wide range of open model families with multiple training methods

tools.name: Modal
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-per-second serverless GPU compute; includes free monthly credits
supported_models: Any open model (Llama, Mistral, Qwen, etc.) via custom code
features: Autoscaling to many GPUs on demand
Integrates with Axolotl and custom pipelines
tools.best_for: Custom, code-first fine-tuning runs that need on-demand serverless GPU scaling without managing clusters

tools.name: Replicate
tools.pricing_paid: Pay per second of training and inference compute; no upfront commitment
supported_models: various open LLMs and vision models
tools.best_for: Developers who want fast, API-driven LoRA fine-tuning and instant hosted deployment

tools.name: Fireworks AI
tools.pricing_paid: Serverless pay-per-token with competitive rates; LoRA fine-tuning and dedicated deployments available
tools.best_for: Latency-sensitive production inference of fine-tuned open models with an OpenAI-compatible API
